text.tspan: Laser cutting guide
Step 2: log in to the laser PC
Step 1: pick the material you want to cut
Step 3: open your file in Inkscape
Log in with username: nolop-machine
Click the icon at the bottom of the screen. You can also install Inkscape for free on your own
computer to prep your cut. Inkscape can import DXF and SVG file types. It is best to export your
files in inches or millimeters.
Nolop Makerspace
Tufts University
Step 4: scaling your design
Step 5: set up lines to cut
The laser can cut most wood, plastic, leather, and rubber up to a thickness of around 3 mm. Our
laser is not powerful enough to cut metal. The bed of the laser is 300 x 600 mm, or around 12
inches x 24 inches. The Nolop store sells 3 mm plywood and acrylic precut to the dimensions of
the bed.
After opening your file, select "Read from file" as the Method of Scaling. If this second window
appears, you can press "OK".
FAQ

tspan.tspan: Why not leave the laser unattended?

text.tspan: Sometimes, the laser sets your material on fire. We have a fire blanket on the side of each laser,
which works great, if you are there to detect the fire. The blanket will not deploy itself.

tspan.tspan: What if I need to cut something really thick or really big?

text.tspan: The laser across the street in Bray is more powerful and has a larger bed.

tspan.tspan: Have any questions not on this guide?

text.tspan: Come up to the staff desk and an employee will be happy to help you!
Laser guide contributors: Yufeng Wu, Jeremy Kanovsky, Brandon Stafford
Aiden Auretto, Sara Murillo
License: Creative Commons BY-SA
Select the lines you want to cut and navigate to the side panel on the right. If the panel is not
present, you can show it by selecting Object > Fill and Stroke... in the ribbon at the top of
Inkscape.
The color and thickness of your lines will tell the laser whether to cut through or just do a shallow
cut on the material. You can set these under the "Fill and Stroke" tab in the side panel.
Visually confirm that you changed your line color and thickness.
Open up UCP (the red box on the taskbar). This software receives the Inkscape file you made in
step 5 and controls the laser itself.
When UCP opens, your file should show up automatically. Cuts are displayed in red, shallow cuts
in blue, and rasters in grayscale.
Unfortunately, the pre-canned settings from the materials database are not always correct and we
have more accurate settings for cutthing through wood and acrylic posted on whiteboards near
each laser.
To set these:
1) Open the "Manual Control" tab of the settings dialog
2) Click on the "Red" color mode
3) Set the proper power and speed for the laser you are using
4) Click "Set"
5) Click "Apply"
6) Click "OK" to close the dialog box
The white canvas that your file is on in UCP represents the laser bed. Make sure that the cuts you
want to make are both on the bed and on the material you are cutting.
There are many ways to do this; we will use a method that relies on the Focus and Relocate View
tools.
1) On the right middle of the screen, click on the "Focus View" tool to show:
A) The current position of the laser head
B) The current position of the mouse relative to the top left corner of the laser bed
Clicking anywhere on the canvas in UCP will drive the head of the laser to that position in the
real world. When the laser cutter's lid is open, the laser will project a red dot straight down onto
the material that you are cutting.
This lets you see exactly where parts of your cut will be by clicking on locations in the canvas.
Any remaining lines or images that do not fit these two criteria will be rastered (the laser will draw
them out by using a back and forth sweeping pattern like a printer).
To cut through change the width to "Hairline"
and the color to pure red (RGB = 255,0,0).

tspan.tspan: to set the fill to No paint.

text.tspan: Under Stroke Style, change all
line widths to "Hairline".
To shallow cut change the width to "Hairline"
and the color to pure blue (RGB = 0,0,255).
Step 6: print your file to the printer called VLS3.60/75
Hit Ctrl-P to print in Illustrator. You should not need to change any settings. Inkscape will foolishly
believe that it is printing to a conventional paper printer, but really, the laser driver will take over!
Note: You might worry that the laser will start up right away. Clicking print will not start the laser,
just send the file we want to cut to the software that controls it.
Step 7: open job in laser control software (UCP)
Step 8: set material and thickness
If your file is not showing up in UCP or the colors are wrong, you can start troubleshooting by
repeating step 6, checking to make sure that the print preview in the bottom left of the print
window looks correct and no errors show up when printing.
Also, double check the line colors from step 5. You also need to ensure the opacity of those lines
is set to 100%.
Step 9: set power and speed for cutting
Step 10: move job to proper location on UCP canvas
Navigate to the settings menu in the bottom right of UCP. This menu contains the settings that
control how powerful the laser is when it is cutting, performing shallow cuts, and rastering.
To set everything up for the material you are using:
1) Click on the "Materials Database" tab at the top of the menu.
2) Select the material you will be cutting from the materials database.
The profile for birch plywood is: Natural > Wood > Medium Wood > Birch
The profile for acrylic is: Plastic > Acrylic > Cast Acrylic > Cast Acrylic
3) Enter the thickness of the material you are cutting (usually 3.00 mm).
4) Select "Apply" to apply the defaults for the selected material.
Focus View
Relocate View
B
A
2) Find a spot on the material you are cutting that you want to be in the top left corner of where
you plan on making your cuts. and move the laser head there. You should see a red dot on your
material where you want the top-left point of your cut to be.
3) Click on the "Focus View" tool.
Notice that some nodes will appear around the file you imported into UCP.
4) Move your file over to the point you picked in step 2.
You can either drag the file by these nodes, or click "To Pointer" in the
bottom right to move the highlighted node directly to the laser head's
current position.
5) Check that all four corners of your cuts are on the laser bed and on the material that you want
to cut by clicking near the corners in the Focus View tool and watching where the red dot moves
in the laser.
It is good practice to bias the points you check by a few millimeters or so outward to ensure
some safety margin.
Check that each red X is not off the bed or over a hole in your material.
Step 11: focus the laser
Use the focusing gauge on the left side of the laser to set the bed height so that the laser is
focused on your material. If the laser is not focused, it might not cut all the way through the piece
you are working on.
Place the black base of the focusing gauge on your material and using the arrows on the control
panel at the front right of the laser, move the bed up and down until the laser head starts to kick
the white part of the gauge to the side.
Note: If you are doing multiple cuts back to back, you do not need to focus the laser each time.
Once at the start of the session and each time you change the thickness of the material you are
cutting is all that are required.

tspan.tspan: Close the lid to the laser.

text.tspan: Go back to UCP and start the laser. This can be done by clicking the green arrow (run button) on
the upper right of the program.
The arrows indicate
which way the bed will
move when pressed.
Focusing Gauge and Laser Head
Move bed up until laser kicks gauge out to the side.
Step 12: start your cut!
